answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed if caught duplicating work or voting twice, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. Reputation then accrues only through attested useful work over time, like pigment slowly staining velvet — it cannot be faked overnight. An attacker at their nadir, with no history and no stake, starts with zero weight, so Sybil volume buys nothing without real cost.
